question: Can conditional phase-response matrices explain smooth but phase-sensitive known-tone responses, and does a source-global mean predict held-out sources better than identity?

design.question: Can conditional phase-response matrices explain smooth but phase-sensitive known-tone responses, and does a source-global mean predict held-out sources better than identity?
design.scope: REUSE ONLY: center signal rows and base forecasts. No hidden states, no extra frequencies/amplitudes, no native inference.
design.coordinate_convention: Input/output coordinates [sin(omega*t),cos(omega*t)], phase at forecast origin. Input coefficients A[cos(phi),sin(phi)]. H columns are opposite-phase central differences projected onto forecast basis and divided by A.
design.primary_projection: Uncentered orthogonal least-squares projection onto exact continuous sine/cosine basis,32 future steps. Also fit a DC nuisance jointly and report H_dc_adjusted, DC coefficients and matrix shift; finite-window leakage is not ignored.
design.decomposition: J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],q=trace(H)/2,r=(H21-H12)/2; H=(qI+rJ)+S, S symmetric traceless. Frobenius energy split only, not a physical waveform-energy attribution. S includes phase conjugation; nonzero S need not imply an eccentric ellipse.
design.rank: Both singular values, axis ratio, participation rank, numerical rank at1e-10*max(1,smax), relative rank at10% of smax with absolute dead floor1e-8. Threshold flags do not prove absent information.
design.residuals: Odd waveform M=[(f0-fpi)/2,(fpi2-f3pi2)/2]/A. Off-frequency residual R=M-BH is orthogonal to B. E=[f0+fpi-2fbase,fpi2+f3pi2-2fbase]. Save raw E, odd M, projection and residual.
design.input_gate: Verify actual FP32 center-minus-background histories against nominal four-phase waveforms; RMS error/peak A must be<=1e-5. Record antipodal input closure; no phase or source is replaced.
design.energy_closure: For every matrix predictor K, phase-energy-pooled NMSE = ||B(H-K)||F^2/||B||F^2 + ||R||F^2/||B||F^2 + ||E||F^2/(4*A^2*||B||F^2). Exact finite-horizon algebra, no stationarity assumption.
baselines: source-global LOSO arithmetic mean H from other15 sources, separately model/policy/frequency
per-source H, fitted on same4 phases: optimistic descriptive in-band ceiling, NOT held-out prediction
design.score: Sum squared waveform errors over all4 phases divided by total ideal signal energy. Equal-source aggregate. Different from earlier unweighted mean of per-phase NMSE because finite-window phase energies differ.
design.resampling: 4096 source bootstrap draws, seed4954200, stratified4 background types with4 sources each. Reuse the same source draws for all models/policies/frequencies/endpoints; phases are never resampling units.
design.inference: Descriptive reused16-source exploratory comparison; percentile95 intervals on source means and paired gains, no corrected confirmation or p-values. All source rows and gain signs retained.
design.primary_comparison: Identity-minus-LOSO waveform NMSE by model/policy/frequency. Per-source H is an explanatory ceiling and cannot establish new-source predictive performance.
design.limitations: Finite horizon and a fixed background break phase/time-shift symmetry. No LTI, global smoothness, cross-model coordinate equivalence, training-causality or absent-information claim. Only4 phases at one amplitude: even response can expose nonlinearity, but full phase orbit is unobserved.

evidence_class: Descriptive conditional behavioral response geometry; LOSO response prediction is distinct from same-source explanatory fit
next_decision: Review proposal-only fresh16-source transfer at the same centers using frozen old mean H. Nearby-frequency/anchoring controls remain optional separately declared work; no native slot used.
interpretation: H is a finite-amplitude conditional odd-response map, fitted on four cardinal phases at one amplitude. It is not an LTI transfer function or a tested full phase orbit.

A large symmetric-traceless component is phase-sensitive or conjugate-linear behavior in these coordinates. Pure phase conjugation can still map a circle to a circle; singular values and determinant disambiguate shape and orientation.
Source-global LOSO scores measure prediction of the model response to a known intervention, not improvement of its forecasting accuracy. Identity encodes ideal continuation semantics.
Per-source H is fitted on the same responses and is an optimistic in-band explanatory ceiling. Its remaining waveform error separates exactly into off-frequency odd response and even response.
Primary sine/cos projection can absorb finite-window DC leakage. The DC-adjusted H and intercept are sensitivity controls, not alternate results selected after seeing outcomes.
leading_interpretation: A reproducible conditional phase-response structure is visible, especially Bolt at19.2h; this challenges a blanket jagged/messy account. TimesFM retains substantial even and off-band response error. Smooth conditional structure is neither time invariance nor correct semantics. LOSO predicts model behavior, not improved forecasts.
